MAJOR: `_load()` returns `{}` for paths escaping the repo root (symlink/`..` traversal) instead of failing closed; that silently skips a changed item and the stderr message mislabels it as "deleted path(s)" — the exact silent-skip class this ticket exists to eliminate.

`_git()` ignores `r.returncode`; a failed `merge-base`/`diff` yields `""` and falls back to `origin/develop` silently, so transitions can be computed against the wrong base and count 0 with no signal. Fail-closed posture must extend to the git plumbing, not just JSON parsing.
`if not cur:` conflates "deleted/absent" with "parseable but falsy/empty" content (`{}`, `[]`), so a corrupt-but-valid-JSON changed item is counted as a deleted path rather than flagged.
MINOR: `_repo_root()` spawns a fresh `git rev-parse` subprocess on every `_load()` call — O(changed-items) subprocesses on large diffs; cache it (module-level/lru_cache) for the scan.
A truthy non-dict item (e.g. `[1]`) raises an unhandled `AttributeError` at `cur.get(...)`, not the fail-closed `RuntimeError` with the path — `json.loads` result should be validated as `dict`.

`product-forge/config/store-registry.json` gains `"BI-TEST-*.json"` with no justification in the acceptance criteria; a bare root-level glob can pull ad-hoc artifacts into the store — confirm intent or drop it.
`print(..., file=sys.stderr)` added without an `import sys` shown in the diff — verify the module already imports `sys`, else the gate crashes on first skipped path.
NIT: `id-blocks.json` bumps `reserved_up_to` 1469→1477 while sessions jump 1469→1477, leaving IDs 1470–1476 unattributed — record why the gap exists to keep the reservation ledger auditable.
Tests use `try/except/else: raise AssertionError` instead of `pytest.raises`; idiomatic and shorter with the fixture.
SUMMARY: Sound fix for the repo-root path resolution with tests covering resolution, deletion skip, traversal, and fail-closed parsing; direction is right.
Top risks: escape/empty paths still silently skipped and misreported as "deleted", and `_git()` swallowing non-zero git exit codes can mask the same class of silent under-count the ticket targets.
Minor cleanups: per-item subprocess, non-dict JSON handling, unexplained store-registry glob, `sys` import verification.
